reference_drawer.title: 📖 Quadratic Equations Reference Guide
reference_drawer.description: Standard form definitions and root verification rules:

items.rule: A quadratic equation in x has the form ax² + bx + c = 0, where a, b and c are real numbers and a is not zero.
A real number α is a root if substituting x = α satisfies the equation.
items.example: For x² - 5x + 6 = 0, x = 2 is a root because the left side becomes zero.

items.rule: After simplification, the highest power with a non-zero coefficient determines the degree.
items.example: An apparently quadratic equation can become linear after cancellation.

items.rule: Substitute the proposed value into the complete left side and compare with zero.
items.example: Evaluate every term before making the final comparison.

items.rule: If a specified value is a root, substitution creates an equation involving the unknown coefficient.
items.example: Solve for k and substitute it back to verify.

concepts.title: 1. Standard Form Definition
concepts.subtitle: Degree, coefficients, and the non-zero leading coefficient
concepts.summary: A quadratic equation has degree 2 and can be written as ax² + bx + c = 0 with a not equal to zero.

points.text: Degree 2: The highest remaining power of x after simplification is 2.
Leading coefficient: The coefficient of x² must be non-zero.
Simplify first: Cancellation can reduce an apparently quadratic equation to a lower degree.

concepts.trap: Calling an equation quadratic before simplifying and checking whether the x² term survives.

concepts.title: 2. Root of a Quadratic
concepts.subtitle: A root makes the equation true
concepts.summary: A number r is a root when substituting x = r makes the complete quadratic expression equal to zero.

points.text: Substitute the candidate into every occurrence of x.
A zero result confirms the candidate is a root.

concepts.trap: Checking only one term or stopping before all terms are combined.

concepts.title: 3. Equivalent Polynomial Forms
concepts.subtitle: Expand, collect, then assess degree
concepts.summary: Bracketed and expanded expressions may represent the same equation; degree must be judged after simplification.

points.text: Bring all terms to one side before final classification.

concepts.trap: Assuming an equation is quadratic merely because x² appears before cancellation.

concepts.title: 4. Checking a Given Root
concepts.subtitle: Substitute, evaluate, compare
concepts.summary: Root verification follows a reliable sequence: substitute, evaluate, and compare the complete result with zero.

points.text: Combine the contributions and compare with zero.

concepts.trap: Sign errors or incomplete evaluation before the final comparison.

concepts.title: 5. Finding an Unknown Coefficient
concepts.subtitle: Use a known root to determine k
concepts.summary: A specified root converts the quadratic into an equation in the unknown coefficient.

points.text: Solve the resulting equation in k.

concepts.trap: Forgetting to substitute the root into every x-term or failing to verify k.
